message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Fresh sweep completed using the monitored product list in Products.txt. I found three credible, product-matched vulnerability groups reported or updated within the daily monitoring window: Google Chrome/Microsoft Edge Chromium updates, MongoDB Server, and Ubiquiti UniFi OS/UID components. Older Microsoft Patch Tuesday, OpenSSL, Redis, Tomcat, SonicWall, Cisco, Fortinet, and VMware items were excluded because their primary disclosures fell outside the 24-hour window or did not cleanly match the monitored products.

**Finding 1: Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge Chromium security updates**

- Product: Google Chrome; Microsoft Edge
- Issue: Chrome Stable Channel 149.0.7827.114/.115 with 28 security fixes, including critical CVE-2026-12007, CVE-2026-12008, CVE-2026-12009, CVE-2026-12010, and CVE-2026-12011, plus multiple high-severity CVEs through CVE-2026-12035. Microsoft also released Edge Stable 149.0.4022.69 on 12 June 2026 incorporating the latest Chromium security updates.
- Severity: Critical and High for the highlighted Chrome CVEs; Edge CVE details were not fully listed by Microsoft at the time checked.
- Description: Google published a desktop Stable Channel update for Windows, macOS, and Linux addressing browser memory-safety, sandbox-escape, input-validation, GPU, Network, Media, Autofill, DevTools, Safe Browsing, and related component issues. Microsoft Edge is relevant because the 12 June stable update incorporates Chromium security updates.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge, and the vendor pages explicitly name those products.
- Sources: Google Chrome Releases https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/06/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_01962725236.html; Microsoft Edge release notes https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnotes-security

**Finding 2: MongoDB Server use-after-free in server-side JavaScript**

- Product: MongoDB Server
- Issue: CVE-2026-11933
- Severity: High; CNA CVSS v3.1 score 8.8 and CVSS v4.0 score 8.7 reported by NVD/MongoDB.
- Description: A use-after-free in MongoDB Server's server-side JavaScript engine can be triggered by an authenticated user with read privileges who can run server-side JavaScript, potentially causing process memory disclosure or a mongod crash.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes MongoDB, and the NVD record explicitly names MongoDB Server and mongod.
- Source: NVD https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-11933

**Finding 3: Ubiquiti UniFi OS and UID Enterprise Agent vulnerabilities**

- Product: Ubiquiti/UniFi OS; UID Enterprise Agent
- Issue: Security Advisory Bulletin 065 related CVEs, including CVE-2026-47368, CVE-2026-47369, CVE-2026-47370, CVE-2026-48610, and CVE-2026-47367.
- Severity: Critical for CVE-2026-47369 and CVE-2026-47370 where CVSS 3.1 score 9.9 is reported; High for CVE-2026-47368 and CVE-2026-48610; CVE-2026-47367 is also reported as Critical in advisory aggregations.
- Description: The UniFi OS issues include path traversal, privilege escalation, command injection, and improper access control that can allow network-accessible attackers, in some cases with low privileges, to obtain data, escalate privileges, execute commands, or make unauthorized changes on affected devices. CVE-2026-47367 affects UID Enterprise Agent rather than UniFi OS itself, but is part of the same Ubiquiti advisory family.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Ubiquiti/UniFi, and the CVE records and advisory references explicitly identify UniFi OS or Ubiquiti UID Enterprise Agent.
- Sources: NVD CVE-2026-47368 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-47368; NVD CVE-2026-47369 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-47369; NVD CVE-2026-48610 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48610; Ubiquiti advisory reference https://community.ui.com/releases/Security-Advisory-Bulletin-065-065/aa46a22b-fc43-4eae-9382-6fc8feda967a

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for Chrome/Edge browser fleets and Ubiquiti/UniFi deployments because the reported severities include critical browser and network-device issues. MongoDB Server should also be reviewed promptly where server-side JavaScript is enabled or available to authenticated users.
